transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-08
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim, Priya Shah, Jordan Lee - Redwood; Marissa Lane, Daniel Cho, Irene Gomez, Samir Naik - Novus Retail

Auto-summary (generated): Quick walkthrough of Redwood structured output JSON mode focusing on schema enforcement, function/tool calling, and guardrails for production use cases. Next steps: pricing, security docs, pilot.

[00:00] Alex Kim: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm alex kim with redwood, i'm the AE, and with me is priya our se and jordan who'll jump in on infra details, how's everyone doing?
[00:05] Marissa Lane: good thanks alex, excited to see the structured output stuff, we have a fairly strict schema for our checkout personalization so this is timely.
[00:12] Priya Shah: awesome, quick agenda - i'll show JSON mode, how we attach schemas, guardrails and then demo function calling to our product catalog api mock. we'll also talk about dedicated capacity and security controls towards the end. sound good?
[00:20] Daniel Cho: yep, perfect. we want to understand failure modes and how you prevent hallucinated product ids and pii leakage.
[00:28] Priya Shah: totally, good callout. i'll start share my screen - please chime if video lags.
[00:35] [screen share starts]
[01:05] Priya Shah: so this is the API console, i'm going to toggle "JSON mode" - what that does is instruct the model to constrain outputs to a provided json schema and we run a validation step server-side. if the model emits invalid json we can either reject, try autocorrect with a second pass, or call a fallback function - we call that the schema_guardrail pipeline.
[01:25] Irene Gomez: when you say autocorrect, is that an automated model edit or some deterministic parser? we've had parsers that mangle nested arrays.
[01:33] Priya Shah: good question - it's a hybrid. first we run a strict json parser; if parsing fails we run a constrained generation pass with the original context plus an instruction to output strictly valid json matching the schema. there's also an option to run a deterministic sanitizer for known classes, like stripping unknown keys.
[01:48] Alex Kim: to add, you can configure the response policy: reject_and_error, autocorrect_and_warn, autocorrect_and_audit - so it maps to your risk profile.
[02:05] Marissa Lane: can you show an example with a product recommendation response? like product_id, score, reasons array.
[02:12] Priya Shah: yep - switching to a demo prompt.
[02:20] [Demo run]
[02:25] Priya Shah: prompt: "Given user history X return top 3 recommendations as json matching schema" - schema pasted here: {
  "type":"object",
  "properties":{
    "recommendations":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"product_id":{"type":"string"},"score":{"type":"number"},"reasons":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}}},"required":["product_id","score"]}},
  "required":["recommendations"]
}
[02:55] [Model call initiated]
[03:10] Priya Shah: okay response came back, console shows parsed json and a validation status OK. here's the structured payload - note we also show a token-level delta so you can see where the model was uncertain, and an audit log entry.
[03:28] Jordan Lee: on infra notes, that validation runs at the control plane in hosted, but for Dedicated and Private we run it inline - lower latency but you get the same enforcement.
[03:42] Daniel Cho: what's the latency impact for that second pass autocorrect?
[03:47] Priya Shah: depends - typical parse+validate is sub 20ms. if we do a second generation pass it's extra model latency similar to a short prompt - for the 3-item responses it's ~150-300ms added in our tests. you can also route autocorrect to a cheaper model family to save cost.
[04:05] Marissa Lane: okay that seems doable. what about function calling? we want the model to call our product availability function and then return merged results in the json.
[04:14] Priya Shah: demo time - we define a function schema in the console, e.g., product_lookup(product_id)->{availability:boolean,warehouse:string,eta_days:int}, and we demo tool calling. i'll wire it to a fake product api.
[04:30] [Function call demo]
[04:35] Priya Shah: when the model emits a function call, we surface it in the trace and automatically call the bound webhook. the function's response gets injected back into the prompt as context for the final json output. here's a live example where the model first generated 3 product ids, we called the product_lookup function for each, and then the final json includes availability.
[05:05] Irene Gomez: how do you prevent the model from inventing product ids and then calling the function on nonsense ids?
[05:12] Priya Shah: a few strategies: pre-filtering against your catalog index (we provide connectors), scoring thresholds to reject low-confidence ids, and a policy to prefer callable functions only for items that exist. also the schema can require availability fields and we can flag mismatches in the audit.
[05:30] Marissa Lane: do you support streaming function calls? we stream partial outputs to our UI.
[05:36] Alex Kim: yes, partial streaming is supported. in streaming mode we can also emit function call intents early and then stream the function responses in subsequent chunks - there's a consistent event model in the SDK.
[05:50] Daniel Cho: security - for hosted, what happens to the product api keys and pii?
[05:56] Jordan Lee: hosted keeps control plane logs; payloads are encrypted in transit and at rest, we offer field-level redaction and optional payload tokenization. for enterprise you can choose Dedicated or Private; Dedicated isolates GPU pools and Private gives you control plane in your VPC. we integrate with KMS/HSM for key management.
[06:20] Marissa Lane: we need SOC2 plus the ability to store logs in our region and a retention policy we can pick. is that in the docs?
[06:28] Alex Kim: yes we'll share SOC2 and ISO certs; for hosted we support region-based logging and retention controls as an add-on. Dedicated gives you contractable retention SLAs.
[06:40] [Demo: Guardrails config]
[06:45] Priya Shah: here's the guardrail panel - you can set response policies, allowed keys in the json, max array sizes, and custom validators (regex, value ranges). we also show a "preflight" mode that runs schema checks on top of your test prompts so you can catch regressions before rollout.
[07:10] Marissa Lane: can we run that preflight against a thousand prompts? we want to batch validate before shipping.
[07:16] Priya Shah: yes, Optimize has a batch eval runner - you can upload prompts and expected schemas and get a regression report with token-level diffs and failure reasons. we can spin that up for your pilot.
[07:30] Daniel Cho: about cost - if we use Dedicated, what's the unit economics vs hosted?
[07:36] Alex Kim: generally Dedicated reduces per-token costs via reserved GPU throughput and more efficient batching, especially for repeated small inference patterns. we'll send you the detailed pricing sheet but ballpark Dedicated is better if you have sustained high throughput; hosted is best for variable traffic and quick ramp.
[07:56] Irene Gomez: what's the onboarding like for Private? we might have compliance teams asking for air-gapped deployments.
[08:04] Jordan Lee: Private can be on-prem or VPC-hosted; the control plane can be in your network, and we provide an operator package. air-gapped requires more integration effort; typical engagements include a 4-6 week onboarding.
[08:20] [Audience question: audit logs]
[08:25] Marissa Lane: how granular are audit logs? do we get token-level traces and schema validation events?
[08:30] Priya Shah: yes, audit logs include model inputs, token-level traces, validation events, function call traces, and policy decisions. retention and export are configurable.
[08:45] [Demo: streaming + function calling trace]
[09:00] Priya Shah: showing a trace where the model streams a partial recommendation, emits a function call for availability, we call the function, and then the final json is emitted. note the trace highlights where the autocorrect step modified the structure.
[09:28] Daniel Cho: interesting. how do you handle fallback if the function webhook is slow or fails?
[09:34] Priya Shah: you can configure retries, timeouts, and fallback policies. e.g., if function call fails we can return a default availability=false and mark the record as degraded, or queue an async enrichment and return partial results. those policies are configurable per route.
[09:55] Marissa Lane: for our use-case the UI expects a deterministic schema quickly, so we'd prefer fail-closed rather than best-effort. can we enforce that?
[10:02] Alex Kim: absolutely - set the policy to reject_on_function_error and the call will fail with an explicit error you can handle client-side.
[10:15] Irene Gomez: about model drift - we need monitoring for quality regressions tied to our prompt set.
[10:20] Priya Shah: Optimize has quality monitoring; you can upload a golden set and we run periodic evals - alert on NPS-like drops or schema failures. we also support canary rollouts of model versions so you can route a percentage of traffic and compare metrics.
[10:38] [Customer asks about SDKs]
[10:40] Alex Kim: SDKs support schema-first calls where you pass a json schema and get back a parsed object; streaming SDK returns events: partial, function_call, function_response, final_json. we have examples in node/python/ruby.
[10:56] Marissa Lane: do you provide connectors to our catalog or do we build them?
[11:00] Jordan Lee: we have built-in connectors for common stores, and for custom catalogs we provide a lightweight adapter. For pilot we can set up a simple s3-backed index.
[11:15] [Performance chat]
[11:18] Priya Shah: important note on KV cache - for session-based personalization we keep a KV cache of key context to avoid re-encoding long histories; Dedicated lets you persist that cache across GPUs for lower cold-start latency.
[11:35] Daniel Cho: are there any gotchas with quantized models and json mode?
[11:40] Priya Shah: quantization is orthogonal - model quality can slightly shift; for structured output we recommend validating with your golden set. Optimize can recommend quantization profiles based on your workload.
[11:55] Marissa Lane: ok i have more internal questions but this is great. what's the proposed pilot?
[12:00] Alex Kim: propose a 1-week pilot: we onboard sample prompts, run preflight on ~1k prompts, spin up a small Dedicated slice or hosted sandbox with trial keys, run functional availability checks and atomic benchmarks comparing latency/cost.
[12:12] Marissa Lane: sounds good. we'll need pricing and the SOC2 docs.
[12:16] Alex Kim: will send.
[12:18] [wrap up]
[12:20] Alex Kim: quick recap: send pricing + certs, provide trial keys, Priya will share schema examples and the demo recording, Marissa will send sample prompts. next call - schedule a pilot kickoff next week. thanks everyone.
[12:35] Marissa Lane: thanks all, bye.
[12:38] [call ends]

Notes on transcription: a few words mis-transcribed by the recorder (e.g., KV cache sometimes "KV cash"), filler words preserved. Speakers sometimes overlap; labels chosen conservatively.
